notes: Focused v1.7.1 correctness regressions for facts corrected after a full reference audit against package registries, changelogs, and tagged sources (Rich, Cobra v1.2+, Wish v2.0.3, lazygit, btop, cli-spinners, tview's concurrency wiki, DO_NOT_TRACK adoption history). Assertions define the grading rubric; improvement claims require a recorded harness run against one immutable skill hash.

evals.name: rich-traceback-install
evals.prompt: I want Rich's pretty tracebacks in my Click CLI. Is `import rich; rich.install()` the right call, and which Python CLIs actually ship Rich so I can point my team at precedent?
assertions: Uses rich.traceback.install() (from rich.traceback import install) rather than a nonexistent rich.install()
Says rich.install() does not exist, or at minimum never presents it as valid
Cites pip as vendoring Rich without claiming Poetry or Sphinx depend on it
Keeps the traceback installer separate from rich.pretty.install(), which only affects REPL output

evals.name: lazygit-config-format
evals.prompt: I'm building a lazygit-style multi-pane tool and want to mirror lazygit's configuration conventions. What file format and location does lazygit use, and does k9s use the same format for its plugins?
assertions: Says lazygit's config is YAML (config.yml) under the XDG config directory
Does not describe lazygit's config as TOML
Says k9s plugins are defined in plugins.yaml
Recommends choosing a config format from the app's own needs rather than presenting one format as the TUI standard

evals.name: reserved-ctrl-s-save
evals.prompt: My editor-like TUI should bind Ctrl+S to save, the way vim and helix do. Is that safe by default?
assertions: Explains that Ctrl+S is XON/XOFF flow control and can freeze the terminal unless flow control is disabled (stty -ixon)
Does not claim vim or helix bind Ctrl+S to save by default
Notes that helix binds Ctrl+S to save_selection, or otherwise corrects the premise
Offers a conventional alternative binding or an explicit opt-in for users who disable flow control

evals.name: btop-refresh-cadence
evals.prompt: I'm designing a btop-style dashboard. btop refreshes its CPU box every 100ms and the process table every 2s, so should every widget in my app run its own timer?
assertions: Corrects the premise: btop uses a single update_ms setting (default 2000) shared by every box
Recommends widget independence for focus, scroll, and layout rather than mandatory per-widget timers
Reserves a separate cadence for widgets whose data source is slow or expensive
Keeps data collection off the render path regardless of cadence

evals.name: wish-v2-session-options
evals.prompt: I'm serving a Bubble Tea v2 app over Wish v2. How do I make styling follow each SSH client's color profile instead of the server's? Should I call bubbletea.MakeRenderer(sess)?
assertions: Says MakeRenderer is not part of the Wish v2 bubbletea middleware
Recommends bubbletea.MakeOptions(sess) or the bubbletea.Middleware handler so input, output, and profile detection follow the client's PTY
Explains that Lipgloss v2 is pure and no longer owns terminal I/O, so per-session renderers are unnecessary
Keeps all Charm v2 modules on the same major version

evals.name: spinner-delay-contract
evals.prompt: For a one-shot CLI that usually finishes in under 50ms but sometimes takes several seconds, should the spinner appear the instant work starts? Which Braille frames should I use?
assertions: Delays the spinner by roughly 100–200ms so near-instant work never flashes an indicator
Sends progress to stderr and suppresses animation when output is not a TTY
Uses the ten-frame cli-spinners dots sequence or states the frame count correctly if it lists frames
Ends with a final state symbol or clears the spinner cleanly

evals.name: tview-goroutine-draw
evals.prompt: In my tview app a background goroutine polls an API and updates a Table. Is it safe to call app.Draw() from that goroutine, and where do tview deadlocks actually come from?
assertions: Routes primitive mutations from goroutines through QueueUpdate or QueueUpdateDraw
Says a bare app.Draw() from a goroutine is safe but does not synchronize data access
Identifies the deadlock as calling Draw, QueueUpdate, or QueueUpdateDraw from inside an event handler on the main goroutine
Does not claim that calling Draw from a goroutine deadlocks

evals.name: do-not-track-adoption
evals.prompt: I'm adding opt-in telemetry to my CLI. Is DO_NOT_TRACK the standard opt-out that Homebrew, Gatsby, and the .NET SDK follow, or should I define my own?
assertions: Says Homebrew, Gatsby, and the .NET SDK did not adopt DO_NOT_TRACK and use their own variables
Names at least one real adopter such as the GitHub CLI, netdata, or tilt
Recommends a tool-specific opt-out (env var plus subcommand) with DO_NOT_TRACK honored as an extra courtesy
Treats the opt-out as an absolute veto that is never itself reported as an event
